channel.title: SROTrac Weekly
channel.description: Weekly editions from the SRO register: rosters, recognition moves, consultations and enforcement signals across India's financial-sector SROs.

item.title: SROTrac Weekly #8: MFIN's member wall quietly sheds ten names; IRDAI buys six more days; FIDC pleads for slower commission cuts
item.description: MFIN redesigned its members page into region-tabbed carousels, and the wall that listed 84 organisations on 11 September lists 74 today — ten names gone, no join or exit dates published, and the page still claims "53 primary members as on March 2025"; IRDAI extended the distribution-reforms comment window from 25 to 31 October after 650+ comments; FIDC, the NBFC SRO, is aggregating member feedback to ask IRDAI for a phased commission reset, arguing sharp cuts would make credit-linked insurance distribution unviable; everywhere else the register is quiet.

item.title: SROTrac Weekly #7: The AA network gets a rate card; SEBI wants bank deposits on one statement; IRDAI's comment window shuts Sunday
item.description: Sahamati's pricing circular puts a meter on the Account Aggregator network from 1 November — lenders pay a split fee covering the bank, the AA and the SRO, customers cannot be charged for sharing their own data, and technology-service middlemen are cut out of the money; SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey told Sahamati's SamvAAd that bank deposits should join the eCAS statement through the same pipe; IRDAI chairman Ajay Seth promises an "orderly transition" on commission caps with comments closing Sunday, 25 October; Sa-Dhan's quarterly numbers show the microfinance book shrinking again while average tickets rise 15%, prompting the SRO's own chief to call for rethinking the ₹3 lakh qualifying-income threshold; and FEDAI posts an impersonation fraud alert on its homepage.

item.title: SROTrac Weekly #6: Sa-Dhan's FY26 scorecard; the insurance councils break their silence; UFF's reply window closes with no reply
item.description: Sa-Dhan's Bharat Microfinance Report 2026 counts a sector that shrank 11% in FY26 but grew 4% sequentially in the March quarter, with the three-lender guardrail now visible in borrower data; IRDAI's distribution reset gets a possible January 2027 start date and both statutory councils are finally engaging — the Life Insurance Council even proposed persistency-linked commissions; RBI will make Account Aggregators interoperable by 31 December 2026; and our right-of-reply to UFF and BSFG over the silent roster exit closed 11 October with neither party responding.

item.title: SROTrac Weekly #5: UFF's first roster exit; FACE's board and its big-lender report
item.description: UFF's published roster drops BSFG Finance (121 to 120) — the second SRO-FT's first roster movement since recognition; FACE elects PhonePe's Hemant Gala and Navi's Rajiv Naresh to its board; FACE's Digital Personal Loans report puts 70% of personal-loan sanction volume with digital NBFCs; IRDAI chairman says the distribution reset is not final, comments open till 25 October.

item.title: SROTrac Weekly #4: The register doubles to 18; IRDAI takes a knife to distribution economics
item.description: The register expands from 9 to 18 SRO bodies across RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and IBBI (774 member orgs); IRDAI's 23 September distribution consultation lands on the two insurance councils the same week they join; SEBI cancels 12 lapsed research analyst registrations.

item.title: SROTrac Weekly #3: UPI gets a price tag; rosters hold steady
item.description: Rosters hold at 642 members, but UPI's zero-fee era ends Oct 15 — 0.4% MDR above ₹2,000 reshapes the economics of SRPA's payment-operator members.

item.title: SROTrac Weekly #2: Register completes at nine SROs; FIMMDA stands up discipline
item.description: All nine RBI-recognised SROs now tracked on SROTrac. FIMMDA constituted its first disciplinary committee; GFF 2026 put regulatory gap-hopping on notice.

item.title: SROTrac Weekly #1 — UFF's licence, FEDAI's transition, and a tracker goes live
item.description: The week India got its second fintech SRO; what the full RBI SRO map looks like; why rosters matter and who won't publish theirs.
